requirements.requirement: Require new user passwords on node1 to be at least 12 characters long
requirements.summary: pwquality.conf was set to minlen=12; pwscore and a real non-root passwd session both rejected an 11-char password with 'shorter than 12 characters' and accepted 12+ char compliant passwords. Baseline (pre-change) showed no such enforcement (8-char minimum only).

requirements.requirement: Require new user passwords on node1 to use at least 3 different character classes
requirements.summary: pwquality.conf was set to minclass=3; pwscore and a real non-root passwd session both rejected 12-char, 2-class passwords ('less than 3 character classes') and accepted a 12-char, 3-class password. Baseline showed a 13-char single-class password was accepted, confirming no prior class enforcement.

requirements.requirement: Policy is enforced end-to-end through the actual PAM/passwd path for a real (non-root) user, not just at the library level
requirements.summary: pam_pwquality is wired via 'requisite' into /etc/pam.d/system-auth and /etc/pam.d/password-auth, and an expect-driven passwd session for a temporary non-root test user directly demonstrated rejection of sub-12-char and sub-3-class passwords and acceptance of a compliant password with 'all authentication tokens updated successfully'.

requirements.requirement: Policy persists and remains correctly enforced across a service-affecting event (node restart)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 910dc564... and healthy policy state were captured, systemctl reboot was issued and acknowledged (connection dropped then recovered), post-restart boot_id 60715179... differed, and pwquality.conf settings, PAM wiring, and pwscore enforcement (reject short/2-class, accept 12+/3-class) were all re-verified identically after the restart. This matches both the fixed before/after boot-identity snapshots and the direct executor evidence.

overall_summary: The task (require new-user passwords on node1 to be ≥12 characters with ≥3 character classes) is fully satisfied. The executor set minlen=12 and minclass=3 in /etc/security/pwquality.conf, confirmed the pre-change baseline lacked this enforcement, and validated both requirements at the libpwquality level (pwscore) and end-to-end through a real non-root PAM passwd session, showing correct rejections and an accepted compliant password. It additionally performed the node-restart evidence protocol correctly: pre-restart boot identity and healthy state, a reboot acknowledgement with connection loss/recovery, a changed post-restart boot identity, and full re-verification that the policy and PAM wiring survived the restart — consistent with the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. Minor hygiene residue (an unremoved config backup file and a reboot log in /tmp) slightly lowers the hygiene score but does not affect task functionality.
limitations: A leftover timestamped backup of pwquality.conf and /tmp/reboot.log were not confirmed removed, though neither affects policy enforcement or system safety.

Verification relied on a temporary local test user rather than every possible new-user creation path (e.g., useradd + passwd by an administrator), though the PAM wiring shown applies uniformly to local users.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor actions were tightly scoped to the task: a temporary test user and the 'expect' package were installed solely to validate the policy end-to-end and were removed afterward (cmd-ad8d853de1f54928, cmd-8aa8838cf94242c9 after a userdel-in-use retry, which is a legitimate corrective step, not an unnecessary mutation). No failed services, unexpected listening sockets, or package-health issues appear in the after_executor snapshot versus after_prepare. Two minor low-risk residues remain unaddressed: a timestamped backup of /etc/security/pwquality.conf created by cmd-0e9f5fef62ac452e was never removed, and /tmp/reboot.log created by the reboot command (cmd-6fe52ea22211453d) persists in the after_executor temp-file inventory. Both are small, non-destructive, non-security-weakening artifacts, so they lower the score only slightly.
